text: Shape is right (volume matches the analytic value up to the small tread haunches that lap onto the column). Now classify the boundary faces by surface type/radius rather than by bounding box, and check the counts.
Face groups match the analytic areas (shaft wall 22.62 − 20×0.01 tread ends = 22.42; floor π(1.2²−0.1²)=4.4925). Export one STL per patch.
Check that the five patches weld into one closed surface, and look at it.
Watertight union (0 free edges). Display the render.
Verify a safe `locationInMesh` inside the fluid, then write the coarse mesh case.
Write the OpenFOAM case dictionaries (coarse: base 0.1 m, surface refinement level 1, treads level 2).
Mesh OK, total volume 13.2305 vs exact 13.2504 (0.15 % low). Check each patch's meshed area against the CAD area, and look at it.
Every patch within 0.5 % of its CAD area, so all 20 treads survived snapping. Render a clipped view of the mesh with patch colours.
The shaft wall hides the interior; clip the internal volume instead to see column, treads and the gaps between them.
Camera was on the wrong side of the cut; view the cut plane from +y.

Coarse mesh is correct. Refine once: treads and column to level 3 (12.5 mm, ~3 cells across a 40 mm tread), shaft wall level 2. Re-run blockMesh first so this cell replays correctly from the background mesh.
`topOpening` is an opening, not a wall — restart with the right patch type before it gets far.
Refined mesh is clean. Final render for the record, then I'll close.

Built the fluid volume directly in metres: shaft cylinder R=1.200 m × 3.000 m tall, minus a R=0.100 m column running the full height, minus 20 tread boxes (0.250 m deep × 0.040 m thick, exposed radial span 0.100→1.200 m = 1.100 m), each rotated 18° and raised 0.150 m from the last, top of tread *i* at 0.15(i+1) so the 20th lands flush with the 3.000 m opening. Tread boxes are extended inward to the axis so they weld into the column (support); outside the column the span is exactly 1.100 m.

Measured against the request, from the geometry itself: turn 18.0000°/tread, rise 0.15000 m, thickness 0.04000 m, depth 0.25000 m, exposed radial length 1.10000 m, 20 treads, top tread top at z=3.0000. Fluid volume 13.2504 m³ vs the analytic 13.2574 minus the small tread haunches that lap onto the column.

Patches were assigned from face geometry type (cylinder radius 1.2 → `shaftWall`, radius 0.1 → `column`, z=0 plane → `floor`, z=3 plane → `topOpening`, everything else → `treads`), not by bounding-box position, and exported as five STLs in `constant/triSurface`; their union has 0 free edges. Mesh: blockMesh box at 0.1 m + snappyHexMesh, treads level 3 (12.5 mm, ~3 cells across a tread), column 2→3, shaft/floor 2, top 1 — 444,325 cells, `Mesh OK`, max non-orthogonality 49.0, max skewness 2.91. Meshed patch areas are within 0.25 % of the CAD areas (treads −0.04 %, so all 20 treads survived snapping); total mesh volume 13.2341 m³, 0.12 % below CAD, which is the chordal error of the faceted cylinders.

Not checked: no boundary layers were added (`addLayers false`), so near-wall spacing is whatever the level-3 cells give; `topOpening` is typed `patch` and the rest `wall`, but no boundary conditions were written.
